supported_facts: The occurrence is reported during the night of 11 January 2026, with an emergency call at approximately 03:50.
Two adjacent commercial targets on Via del Progresso are described in the same immediate police intervention.
Reporting describes a physically and temporally continuous sequence from the first premises toward the adjacent outlet.
The later pursuit, hiding and arrest are procedural consequences and not separate crime-occurrence geography.

event_identity_analysis.rationale: The sources support a contiguous sequence, adjacent targets and one uninterrupted intervention. There is presently no material temporal or spatial discontinuity justifying two canonical EVENT IDs.
event_identity_analysis.split_condition: Split only if a primary occurrence record later establishes independently completed episodes separated by a meaningful temporal/spatial break.

temporal_analysis.caution: Use exact datetime only if a primary source supports the clock time as occurrence time rather than call/intervention time.

offence_analysis.reported_family: aggravated theft/burglary involving commercial and residential premises
offence_analysis.modelling_note: Multiple targets do not by themselves require multiple EVENT records; offence instances and target locations can remain one-to-many within the continuous episode.

recommended_resolution: Treat as one continuous_episode candidate with multiple target locations/offence assertions. Keep arrest/pursuit geography separate. Do not finalise a reviewed bundle until a primary occurrence source is resolved.
